explanation: TFTP is a minimal protocol on UDP port 69 with no login and no directory listing; it relies on its own block acknowledgments for reliability. FTP uses TCP port 21 for control and a separate data connection (port 20 in active mode), requires a username and password, and supports directory commands. Neither protocol encrypts data; SFTP or SCP is needed for that.

stem: A switch vendor's advisory states that firmware 9.2 does not validate input sent to its web management page. A week later, a public Python script appears that sends a crafted request to that page and returns an administrator session. In security terms, what is the Python script?
choices: A vulnerability
An exploit
A threat
A mitigation
explanation: An exploit is the code or technique that takes advantage of a vulnerability, which is exactly what the script does. The missing input validation in the firmware is the vulnerability, not the script. A threat is the potential for someone or something to use that weakness against an asset, and a mitigation is a control that reduces the risk, such as patching or restricting access to the management page.

stem: During a quarterly test, the security team sends harmless look-alike invoice emails to all staff. 31 percent of recipients click the link and 12 percent type their credentials into the fake page. Which security program element should the company expand first to address this result?
choices: Physical access control at building entrances
A user awareness program that teaches staff to recognize and report phishing
AAA accounting on network devices
Port security on access switch ports
explanation: The test measures how people react to phishing, so the gap is human behavior, which a user awareness program targets with simulated campaigns, reminders and clear reporting steps. Physical access control protects doors and rooms, not inboxes. AAA accounting only records what authenticated users did on devices, and port security limits MAC addresses on switch ports; neither stops a user from typing a password into a fake site.

stem: A company is replacing password-only sign-in for its remote access VPN. Which two sign-in methods qualify as multifactor authentication? (Choose two.)
choices: A password plus the answer to a stored security question
A smart card holding a user certificate, unlocked with a PIN
A password plus a one-time code from an authenticator app on the user's phone
A fingerprint scan plus a face scan
A long passphrase that must be changed every 60 days
explanation: Multifactor authentication combines factors from different categories: something you know, something you have and something you are. A smart card (have) with a PIN (know) and a password (know) with a code from a phone app (have) both mix two categories. A password plus a security answer is two knowledge factors, and a fingerprint plus a face scan is two inherence factors, so neither is multifactor. A long, expiring passphrase is still a single factor.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer entered these commands on a new branch router. A colleague then connects to the console. What happens when the colleague types enable at the R-EDGE1> prompt?
exhibit:
R-EDGE1(config)# enable password Branch!Old
R-EDGE1(config)# enable secret Edge#2026
R-EDGE1(config)# service password-encryption
R-EDGE1(config)# line console 0
R-EDGE1(config-line)# password Con$ole1
R-EDGE1(config-line)# login
R-EDGE1(config-line)# end
choices: Either Branch!Old or Edge#2026 is accepted, because both commands are in the configuration
Only Branch!Old is accepted, because it was configured first
Only Edge#2026 is accepted, because the enable secret takes precedence over the enable password
No password is needed, because service password-encryption disables the enable password
explanation: When both enable password and enable secret are configured, IOS uses only the enable secret, so Edge#2026 is the only value that works. The order the commands were entered does not matter. service password-encryption only obscures plaintext passwords (such as the console and enable password) with reversible type 7 encoding; it does not remove or disable any password, and it has no effect on the already hashed enable secret.

stem: A router's running configuration shows the console and vty line passwords in clear text. Enter the global configuration command that makes IOS store those passwords in type 7 encoded form.
explanation: service password-encryption applies weak, reversible type 7 encoding to plaintext passwords in the configuration, such as line passwords, the enable password and username password entries. It only stops casual shoulder surfing of the config. It does not affect enable secret or username secret, which are already stored as one-way hashes.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. Which source host can successfully ping the server at 10.20.20.10?
exhibit:
R1 interfaces:
  G0/0  10.10.10.1/24   (user LAN)
  G0/1  10.20.20.1/24   (server LAN, server 10.20.20.10)
  G0/2  198.51.100.2/30 (Internet)

R1# show running-config | section access-list|interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 10.20.20.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group 15 out
access-list 15 deny   10.10.10.64 0.0.0.31
access-list 15 permit 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255
choices: 172.16.4.20 (arriving from the Internet)
explanation: The wildcard 0.0.0.31 on 10.10.10.64 matches 10.10.10.64 through 10.10.10.95, so .65 and .94 hit the deny entry when their packets leave G0/1. 10.10.10.96 is outside that block and matches the permit for 10.10.10.0/24. 172.16.4.20 matches neither entry and is dropped by the implicit deny any at the end of every ACL. Return traffic from the server enters G0/1 inbound, which has no ACL, so the replies are not filtered.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. Host 192.168.10.44 sits on the LAN attached to G0/0 of R2. Which two traffic flows from this host are permitted by the ACL? (Choose two.)
exhibit:
R2# show running-config | section USERS-IN|interface GigabitEthernet0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group USERS-IN in
ip access-list extended USERS-IN
 10 deny   tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.50.1.25 eq 22
 20 permit tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 10.50.1.0 0.0.0.255 eq 443
 30 permit udp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.50.1.53 eq domain
 40 permit icmp any any echo
choices: An HTTPS session to 10.50.1.25
An SSH session to 10.50.1.30
A DNS query over TCP port 53 to 10.50.1.53
A ping to 10.50.1.25
A DNS query over UDP port 53 to 10.50.1.54
explanation: Entry 10 denies only TCP port 22 to 10.50.1.25, so HTTPS to that host falls through to entry 20, which permits TCP 443 to all of 10.50.1.0/24. The ping matches entry 40, and the echo replies leave G0/0 outbound, where no ACL is applied. SSH to 10.50.1.30 matches no permit and hits the implicit deny. Entry 30 permits only UDP to 10.50.1.53, so a TCP DNS query to that host and a UDP query to 10.50.1.54 are both dropped by the implicit deny.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. ACL MGMT-FILTER is applied inbound on the R3 interface that faces the user VLANs. Which conclusion is supported by the output?
exhibit:
R3# show access-lists MGMT-FILTER
Extended IP access list MGMT-FILTER
    10 permit tcp 10.99.0.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 22 (148 matches)
    20 deny tcp any any eq 22 (37 matches)
    30 deny tcp any any eq telnet (12 matches)
    40 permit ip any any (5021 matches)
choices: 37 packets with TCP destination port 22 from sources outside 10.99.0.0/24 were dropped
12 Telnet sessions from 10.99.0.0/24 were permitted
148 separate SSH sessions from 10.99.0.0/24 have been set up
Entry 40 can be removed with no effect, because an ACL ends with an implicit permit
explanation: ACL match counters count packets, not sessions. Any SSH packet from 10.99.0.0/24 matches entry 10 first, so the 37 matches on entry 20 must be SSH packets from other sources, and they were dropped. Entry 30 is a deny, so Telnet traffic was dropped, not permitted. Every ACL ends with an implicit deny, so removing entry 40 would drop all the traffic it currently permits.

stem: An extended ACE must match every host in 172.16.32.0/20 as the source. Enter the wildcard mask to use with 172.16.32.0.
explanation: A /20 mask is 255.255.240.0, and the wildcard is its inverse: 255.255.255.255 minus 255.255.240.0 gives 0.0.15.255. That wildcard matches 172.16.32.0 through 172.16.47.255. A common mistake is 0.0.16.255, which is not a contiguous wildcard for this block.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. A lab bench port connects a small unmanaged switch. Two instruments on it have worked for months. A third instrument was added yesterday and cannot reach the network, while the original two still work. Which statement explains the behavior?
exhibit:
SW2# show port-security interface GigabitEthernet1/0/14
Port Security              : Enabled
Port Status                : Secure-up
Violation Mode             : Restrict
Aging Time                 : 0 mins
Aging Type                 : Absolute
SecureStatic Address Aging : Disabled
Maximum MAC Addresses      : 2
Total MAC Addresses        : 2
Configured MAC Addresses   : 0
Sticky MAC Addresses       : 2
Last Source Address:Vlan   : 3c52.82a1.77f0:30
Security Violation Count   : 26
choices: The port is err-disabled and needs shutdown and no shutdown before any device can communicate
The two sticky addresses fill the maximum of 2, so frames from the third MAC are dropped and counted as violations while the port stays up
The aging time of 0 minutes removes secure addresses immediately, so the third device is learned and removed in a loop
The port is in protect mode, so it drops the frames without counting them
explanation: The maximum is 2 and both slots hold sticky addresses, so any frame from a third source MAC is a violation. In restrict mode the switch drops those frames, increments the Security Violation Count (26 here) and can send a syslog or SNMP notification, but the port stays Secure-up, which is why the original instruments still work. The port is not err-disabled; that only happens in shutdown mode. An aging time of 0 means aging is disabled, and protect mode would not increment the counter.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. A user plugs a home router with its DHCP server enabled into Gi1/0/9 on SW-A. Which two statements describe how SW-A handles DHCP in VLAN 30? (Choose two.)
exhibit:
SW-A (access switch, all user ports in VLAN 30)
  Gi1/0/24 = uplink to the distribution switch, which relays to the corporate DHCP server

SW-A# show running-config | include ^ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan 30
ip dhcp snooping
SW-A# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet1/0/9
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/9
 switchport access vlan 30
 switchport mode access
end
SW-A# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24
 switchport mode trunk
 ip dhcp snooping trust
end
choices: DHCPOFFER messages from the home router on Gi1/0/9 are dropped, because that port is untrusted
DHCPDISCOVER messages from clients on untrusted access ports are dropped until those ports are trusted
When a client gets a lease from the corporate server through Gi1/0/24, SW-A records the client MAC, IP, lease, VLAN and access port in the binding table
SW-A compares ARP replies arriving on Gi1/0/9 with the binding table and drops any that do not match
Gi1/0/24 must also have a DHCP rate limit, or the corporate server's replies are dropped
explanation: With DHCP snooping enabled, every port is untrusted unless configured otherwise, and server messages such as OFFER and ACK arriving on an untrusted port are dropped, which blocks the rogue home router. Client messages such as DISCOVER and REQUEST are allowed on untrusted ports, and when the legitimate server's ACK comes back through trusted Gi1/0/24, the switch builds a binding entry. Checking ARP against the binding table is Dynamic ARP Inspection, which is not enabled here. Rate limiting is optional and is not required for trusted ports to work.

stem: Match each AAA function to the event that is an example of it.
pairs: A RADIUS server checks the username and one-time code a contractor enters at the VPN sign-in prompt
A TACACS+ server lets a help desk user run show commands but rejects configure terminal
A TACACS+ server logs each command an administrator enters on a core switch, with a timestamp
distractors: A switch drops a frame because its source MAC exceeds the port security maximum
A router encrypts traffic to a branch office inside an ESP tunnel
explanation: Authentication proves identity (who you are), so verifying a username and one-time code is authentication. Authorization decides what an authenticated user may do, such as allowing show commands but not configuration mode. Accounting records what users did, such as command logs with timestamps. Port security and IPsec ESP are security features, but neither is one of the three AAA functions.

stem: A company connects 40 branch offices to headquarters across the Internet with site-to-site IPsec VPNs that terminate on the branch routers. Which statement describes how a packet from a branch PC to a headquarters server is handled?
choices: The PC must run VPN client software that builds its own IPsec tunnel to headquarters
The PC sends a normal unencrypted packet to its default gateway, and the branch router encrypts and encapsulates it in ESP toward the headquarters VPN gateway
The branch router wraps the packet in GRE, and GRE provides the encryption across the Internet
The branch router opens a TLS session to headquarters for each user who signs in
explanation: In a site-to-site VPN, the VPN gateways (routers or firewalls) build the tunnel, so end hosts send ordinary traffic and need no client software. The branch router protects the packet with IPsec ESP and the headquarters gateway decrypts it. Per-user client software and per-user TLS sessions describe a remote access VPN. GRE provides encapsulation only, with no encryption, which is why GRE over IPsec is used when both are needed.

stem: A penetration tester captured the four-way handshake from a warehouse WLAN that uses WPA2-Personal and is now running an offline dictionary attack against the passphrase. Which change best protects the WLAN against this type of attack?
choices: Keep WPA2-Personal, but change the cipher from AES-CCMP to TKIP
Move to WPA3-Personal, which uses SAE instead of the WPA2 PSK exchange
Disable SSID broadcast so the handshake cannot be captured
Enable MAC address filtering on the WLAN
explanation: WPA3-Personal replaces the WPA2 pre-shared key exchange with Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE), which resists offline dictionary attacks and adds forward secrecy. TKIP is older and weaker than AES-CCMP. Hiding the SSID does not stop handshake capture, because the SSID and handshake are still visible when clients connect. MAC filtering is easily bypassed by spoofing and does nothing to protect the passphrase.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer created a WLAN for handheld scanners on an AireOS WLC. The scanners are set for WPA2-Personal with the correct passphrase, but none can join. Which change fixes the problem?
exhibit:
WLANs > Edit 'WH-SCAN'
General tab
  Profile Name ............ WH-SCAN
  SSID .................... WH-SCAN
  Status .................. [x] Enabled
  Interface/Interface Group  scanners-vlan40
  Broadcast SSID .......... [x] Enabled
Security tab > Layer 2
  Layer 2 Security ........ WPA+WPA2
  WPA Policy .............. [ ]
  WPA2 Policy ............. [x]   WPA2 Encryption: [x] AES  [ ] TKIP
  Authentication Key Management
    802.1X ................ [x] Enable
    PSK ................... [ ] Enable
Security tab > AAA Servers
  Authentication Servers .. None
choices: Check TKIP under WPA2 Encryption so older scanners can negotiate a cipher
Under Authentication Key Management, disable 802.1X, enable PSK, set the PSK format to ASCII and enter the passphrase
Change the interface from scanners-vlan40 to the management interface
Set Layer 3 Security to Web Policy so the scanners authenticate with a portal
explanation: A new AireOS WLAN defaults to WPA2 with AES and 802.1X key management, which needs a RADIUS server, and none is assigned. For WPA2-Personal, PSK must be enabled under Authentication Key Management, with the format (usually ASCII) and passphrase entered, and 802.1X cleared. The scanners already support AES, so adding TKIP fixes nothing and weakens security. The interface only maps the WLAN to a VLAN, and a Layer 3 web policy is a captive portal, not WPA2-PSK.

stem: An audit of the access switches produced the findings below. Match each security term to the finding that is an example of it.
pairs: The switches still accept Telnet, which sends administrator credentials in clear text
A criminal group known to target biotech companies is scanning the company's public address space
A tool that captures Telnet logins from the wire and replays them to sign in to a switch
Configuring transport input ssh on all vty lines
explanation: A vulnerability is a weakness, here the use of cleartext Telnet. A threat is the potential danger to an asset, such as an active attacker group targeting the company. An exploit is the tool or method that takes advantage of the weakness, here capturing and replaying Telnet credentials. A mitigation reduces the risk, and limiting vty access to SSH removes the cleartext weakness.

stem: A new data center room requires staff to badge in, enter a PIN, and pass through an access control vestibule that lets only one person through at a time. Which security program element do these measures belong to?
choices: User awareness
User training
Physical access control
AAA accounting
explanation: Badge readers, PIN pads and access control vestibules (often called mantraps) limit who can physically reach equipment, which is physical access control. User awareness and user training focus on what people know and how they behave, such as spotting phishing. AAA accounting records actions on network devices, not entry into rooms.

stem: A security architect wants network administrators to prove their identity to a management system by using a private key on their laptop that matches a public key signed by the company's certificate authority, so that no shared password is used. Which password alternative is this?
choices: Biometrics
Digital certificates
Stricter password complexity rules
Shorter password expiration intervals
explanation: Certificate-based authentication proves identity with a private key that corresponds to a CA-signed certificate, so no password is sent or shared. Biometrics use a physical trait such as a fingerprint. Complexity rules and expiration intervals are password management policies that still depend on a password.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. The vty line password on DSW1 was set to Vty!2026. An administrator opens an SSH session to DSW1. Which statement describes the login?
exhibit:
DSW1# show running-config | include username|enable
enable secret 9 $9$nhEmQVczB7dqsO$X2ZwbDY4Fm6RjUq0hQx4Ksu5oPl8sZ1TnJyC7vAqWeT
username netops privilege 15 secret 9 $9$Lr8pYc3TbWq1Zu$a7Kd0mFzQ2xEw9HnUoP5sVyRcB3tJg6LiN1kM4eXhDs
DSW1# show running-config | section line vty
line vty 0 15
 password 7 08175857484B554544
 login local
 transport input ssh
choices: Any username is accepted, as long as the administrator enters the line password Vty!2026
The administrator must enter the line password first and then the netops secret
The administrator signs in as netops with that account's secret and lands directly in privileged EXEC mode; the line password is not used
The login fails, because transport input ssh requires the login command instead of login local
explanation: login local tells the vty lines to authenticate against the local username database, so the password under the line is ignored. Because netops has privilege 15, a successful login goes straight to privileged EXEC (DSW1#) without the enable secret. SSH sign-in uses a username, which login local provides, so login local is the normal pairing with transport input ssh, not a conflict.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. Security wants the 198.51.100.0/24 network blocked from reaching the web server 172.20.5.10, but logs show 198.51.100.77 still completes HTTPS sessions. Which configuration change makes the block effective without disrupting other users?
exhibit:
R4# show ip access-lists WEB-DMZ
Extended IP access list WEB-DMZ
    10 permit tcp any host 172.20.5.10 eq www (1532 matches)
    20 permit tcp any host 172.20.5.10 eq 443 (8841 matches)
    30 deny ip 198.51.100.0 0.0.0.255 any
    40 permit icmp any any echo-reply (96 matches)
R4# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/2
interface GigabitEthernet0/2
 description DMZ
 ip address 172.20.5.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group WEB-DMZ out
choices: In ip access-list extended WEB-DMZ mode, enter 5 deny ip 198.51.100.0 0.0.0.255 any
In ip access-list extended WEB-DMZ mode, enter deny ip 198.51.100.0 0.0.0.255 any
Change ip access-group WEB-DMZ out to ip access-group WEB-DMZ in on G0/2
Replace entry 30 with 30 deny ip host 198.51.100.77 any
explanation: ACL entries are processed top down and the first match wins, so HTTPS from 198.51.100.77 matches entry 20 and is permitted before entry 30 is checked. Adding the deny with sequence number 5 places it ahead of the permits. An entry without a sequence number is appended at the end (as 50), so it changes nothing. Applying the ACL inbound on G0/2 would filter traffic coming from the DMZ instead of traffic to it, and narrowing entry 30 to one host still leaves it below the permits.

stem: A standard ACL must meet these goals: host 10.40.7.25 is denied, the rest of 10.40.7.0/24 is permitted, the rest of 10.40.0.0/16 is denied, and all other sources are permitted. Put the entries in the order they must appear in the ACL.
items: deny host 10.40.7.25
permit any
explanation: IOS checks ACEs from the top and stops at the first match, so more specific entries must come before broader ones that overlap them. The host deny must come before the /24 permit, or the host would be permitted. The /24 permit must come before the /16 deny, or the whole /24 would be denied. permit any must be last, because placed anywhere earlier it would match everything after it.

stem: A named extended ACL called GUEST-FILTER must filter traffic that arrives on interface G0/3 from the guest network. Enter the interface configuration command that applies it.
explanation: ip access-group <name|number> in applies an IPv4 ACL to packets entering the interface, and out applies it to packets leaving. The keyword access-class is used instead to apply an ACL to vty lines, and ip access-list is the global command that creates or edits the ACL itself.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. ACL 120 is applied inbound on the R5 interface that faces 10.30.0.0/16. The help desk reports that users in 10.30.8.0/24 can still open RDP sessions to servers in 10.40.50.0/24. What is the cause?
exhibit:
R5# show access-lists 120
Extended IP access list 120
    10 permit ip 10.30.0.0 0.0.255.255 any (8812 matches)
    20 deny tcp 10.30.8.0 0.0.0.255 10.40.50.0 0.0.0.255 eq 3389
    30 deny ip any any log (64 matches)
choices: Entry 10 matches all IP traffic from 10.30.0.0/16, including 10.30.8.0/24, so RDP packets are permitted before entry 20 is evaluated
The wildcard 0.0.0.255 in entry 20 matches only addresses that end in .255
ACL 120 is in the standard ACL number range, so the port number in entry 20 is ignored
Entry 20 needs the established keyword to match RDP sessions
explanation: Entry 20 shows no matches because every packet it was meant to catch already matched entry 10, which permits all IP from 10.30.0.0/16 and includes 10.30.8.0/24. The fix is to place the RDP deny before the broad permit. A wildcard of 0.0.0.255 matches any value in the last octet. Numbers 100 to 199 (and 2000 to 2699) are extended ACLs, and the established keyword matches only return TCP segments with ACK or RST set, which would not help here.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. DHCP snooping and Dynamic ARP Inspection are enabled for VLAN 20 on SW1, and no ARP ACLs are configured. A label printer with a statically configured address of 10.20.20.200 (MAC 0050.56a1.4401) is connected to untrusted port Gi1/0/7. The printer cannot communicate, and DAI drop counters for VLAN 20 are increasing. Which statement explains the problem?
exhibit:
SW1# show ip dhcp snooping binding
MacAddress          IpAddress        Lease(sec)  Type           VLAN  Interface
------------------  ---------------  ----------  -------------  ----  --------------------
00:50:56:A1:10:22   10.20.20.51      77012       dhcp-snooping   20    GigabitEthernet1/0/5
00:50:56:A1:33:9C   10.20.20.52      80144       dhcp-snooping   20    GigabitEthernet1/0/6
Total number of bindings: 2
choices: DHCP snooping drops all IP packets from hosts that have no binding entry
DAI finds no binding for the printer's IP and MAC on an untrusted port, so it drops the printer's ARP packets
DAI permits only ARP replies on untrusted ports, so the printer's ARP requests are dropped
Port security on Gi1/0/7 has reached its maximum because the printer has no lease
explanation: DAI checks the sender IP and MAC in ARP packets that arrive on untrusted ports against the DHCP snooping binding table (and any ARP ACLs). The printer used a static address, so it never created a binding, and its ARP packets are dropped. The usual fix is an ARP ACL applied with ip arp inspection filter, or a static binding. Dropping all IP traffic from hosts without bindings is IP Source Guard, not DHCP snooping, and DAI validates both ARP requests and replies.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. The kiosk PC on Gi1/0/22 was learned as a sticky address. A visitor unplugs the kiosk and connects a laptop to the same port. Which two statements are true? (Choose two.)
exhibit:
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/22
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 50
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 1
 switchport port-security mac-address sticky
choices: The port goes into the err-disabled state, because the default violation mode is shutdown
The port stays up and silently drops the laptop's frames, because the default violation mode is protect
After the laptop is removed, an administrator must enter shutdown and then no shutdown on the port (unless errdisable recovery is configured)
The kiosk's sticky address ages out after the default 5 minutes, and the laptop is then learned
The laptop's MAC address replaces the kiosk's sticky entry in the running configuration
explanation: No violation mode is configured, so the default shutdown mode applies and the laptop's frame puts the port into err-disabled. Recovery is manual with shutdown and no shutdown, unless errdisable recovery for psecure-violation is enabled. Sticky addresses stay in the running configuration when the link goes down, and the default aging time is 0 (aging disabled), so the kiosk's entry is neither aged out nor replaced.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. The TACACS+ server ISE-1 is up and reachable. An engineer opens an SSH session to the switch and signs in as breakglass with the correct local secret. The breakglass account does not exist on ISE-1, so the server rejects the login. What is the result?
exhibit:
aaa new-model
!
tacacs server ISE-1
 address ipv4 10.99.5.20
 key 7 13061E010803557878
!
aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group tacacs+ local
!
username breakglass privilege 15 secret 9 $9$Qw7rTzK2pLm0Vc$H3yNfB8sD1xUa5GkJ9eRoW2iZtC6qMvP4lYhE0nXbSu
!
line vty 0 15
 login authentication VTY-AUTH
 transport input ssh
choices: The switch falls back to the local database, and the breakglass login succeeds
The login fails, because the local method is tried only when the TACACS+ server does not respond
The switch checks the local database first, because local accounts are always preferred
The login succeeds at user EXEC, and the engineer must then enter the enable secret
explanation: In an AAA method list, IOS moves to the next method only when the current method returns an error, such as no response from the server. A reject (FAIL) from a reachable TACACS+ server ends the process, so the login fails even though the local account exists. Methods are tried in the order listed, so local comes after TACACS+. The local account is meant as a fallback for when ISE-1 is unreachable.

stem: An engineer is choosing VPN technologies for branch offices and traveling staff. Which two statements are true? (Choose two.)
choices: ESP can provide confidentiality, integrity and authentication, while AH provides integrity and authentication without encryption
In a site-to-site IPsec VPN, every end host at both sites must run VPN client software
A remote access VPN can be built with either IPsec or TLS, such as Cisco Secure Client (AnyConnect) using TLS
GRE encrypts traffic by itself, so IPsec is not needed when GRE tunnels cross the Internet
After the tunnel is up, IKE carries the encrypted user data packets between the peers
explanation: ESP can encrypt and authenticate the payload, while AH authenticates and checks integrity but does not encrypt. Remote access VPNs run from client software on the user's device and can use TLS or IPsec. Site-to-site VPNs are built between gateways, so hosts need no client. GRE has no encryption, which is why it is often protected with IPsec. IKE negotiates keys and security associations, and ESP or AH carries the user data.

stem: A company wants each employee to join the corporate WLAN with their own directory credentials, so that one person's access can be revoked without changing anything for anyone else. Which wireless security option meets this requirement?
choices: WPA3-Personal with SAE
WPA2-Enterprise using 802.1X with a RADIUS server
WPA2-Personal with AES-CCMP
An open WLAN with MAC address filtering
explanation: The Enterprise modes of WPA2 and WPA3 use 802.1X and EAP, with a RADIUS server checking each user's own credentials, so a single account can be disabled. Both Personal modes, with SAE or with a PSK, rely on one shared passphrase, so removing one person means changing it for everyone. MAC filtering on an open WLAN gives no encryption and is easy to bypass by spoofing a MAC address.

stem: On an AireOS WLC (for example, a 3504), match each WLAN setting to the WLAN edit tab where it is configured.
pairs: Interface/Interface Group that maps the WLAN to VLAN 40
PSK format and passphrase for WPA2-Personal
Platinum level for a voice WLAN
explanation: On the AireOS WLAN edit page, the General tab holds the profile name, SSID, status and the interface that ties the WLAN to a VLAN. Security > Layer 2 holds WPA/WPA2 policy, ciphers and the PSK, while Security > AAA Servers selects RADIUS servers. QoS holds the Platinum, Gold, Silver or Bronze level, and Advanced holds options such as session timeout. Security > Layer 3 is for web authentication policies, which none of these settings need.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. After DHCP snooping was enabled on SW3, clients in VLAN 10 stopped getting addresses. The DHCP server is reached through uplink Gi1/0/48, and no interfaces have snooping commands. Enter the interface configuration command needed on Gi1/0/48.
exhibit:
SW3# show running-config | include dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan 10,20
ip dhcp snooping
SW3# show ip dhcp snooping statistics
 Packets Forwarded                                     = 412
 Packets Dropped                                       = 1290
 Packets Dropped From untrusted ports                  = 1290
explanation: Once DHCP snooping is enabled, every port is untrusted by default, and DHCP server messages (OFFER, ACK) arriving on an untrusted port are dropped, which matches the drop counters. Configuring ip dhcp snooping trust on the uplink toward the legitimate server lets those replies through while user ports stay untrusted. ip arp inspection trust is the separate trust setting for Dynamic ARP Inspection.

stem: An audit of 400 branch switches finds that 37 of them have SNMP and NTP settings that no longer match the corporate standard, mostly from one-off fixes made at the CLI. Which approach both corrects these switches and keeps the drift from returning?
choices: Assign one engineer per region to compare each switch's running configuration with the standard every month.
Back up every running configuration to a TFTP server each night.
Store the standard settings as a template in a central source of truth and use an automation tool to push it and regularly check every switch against it.
Send all switch syslog messages at the debugging level to a central server.
explanation: Automation applies one definition of the intended configuration to every device the same way, and scheduled compliance checks find and fix drift before it spreads. Manual monthly reviews are slow and repeat the human error that caused the drift. Nightly backups preserve the drifted configurations but correct nothing, and verbose syslog may show that a change happened but does not enforce the standard.

stem: Which two statements describe controller-based networking compared with traditional device-by-device networking? (Choose two.)
choices: Policy is defined once on the controller, which programs the devices through southbound interfaces.
The controller offers northbound APIs that let scripts and applications manage the whole network through one interface.
Each device is configured individually at its own CLI, and its control plane works with no central view of the network.
Every user data packet must pass through the controller before it is forwarded.
Routing protocols cannot be used anywhere in a controller-based network.
explanation: A controller centralizes configuration and policy, pushes it to devices with southbound protocols such as NETCONF, SSH or OpenFlow, and exposes northbound REST APIs for automation. Per-device CLI configuration with only distributed control planes describes the traditional model. Devices still forward user traffic in their own data planes, and many controller-based designs, such as SD-Access, run a routing protocol in the underlay.

stem: Match each activity to the plane or API it belongs to.
pairs: OSPF routers exchanging LSAs to build their LSDBs
A switch looking up a destination MAC address and sending the frame out one port
An engineer polling a router with SNMP and logging in over SSH
A Python script asking Catalyst Center for the device inventory over a REST API
Catalyst Center pushing configuration to a switch with NETCONF
explanation: The control plane builds the information used for forwarding (routing protocols, STP, ARP). The data plane forwards the actual frames and packets. The management plane covers how people and tools reach the device, such as SSH, SNMP and syslog. A northbound API faces up from the controller toward applications and scripts, while a southbound API faces down toward the network devices.

stem: The exhibit summarizes a packet captured on a routed link between two fabric switches in an SD-Access campus. Which statement correctly describes it?
exhibit:
Frame 2241: 1 packet captured on link EDGE-1 Te1/1/1 <-> INTERMEDIATE-1 Te1/0/4
  Outer IPv4: src 10.0.255.11  dst 10.0.255.12   (Loopback0 of EDGE-1 and EDGE-2)
  Outer UDP:  dst port 4789
  VXLAN:      VNI 4099
  Inner Ethernet + IPv4: src 172.16.20.15  dst 172.16.30.22
  Inner TCP:  dst port 443
choices: The inner addresses belong to the underlay, because they are the real host addresses the switches route on.
The underlay routing protocol must carry routes for 172.16.20.0/24 and 172.16.30.0/24 so this packet can be delivered.
VXLAN is the underlay protocol, and the routed link between the switches is the overlay.
The outer addresses belong to the underlay and identify the tunnel endpoints, while the inner addresses are the endpoints carried in the overlay.
explanation: The underlay is the physical network and its routing, which only needs reachability between switch loopbacks (here 10.0.255.11 and 10.0.255.12). The overlay is the VXLAN tunnel built on top of it, which carries endpoint traffic (172.16.x.x) and its segment ID (VNI) across the fabric. Because endpoint packets are encapsulated, transit switches route on the outer header and do not need routes to the endpoint subnets.

stem: A NOC wants a tool that studies a year of interface utilization and error counters and warns that a WAN link is likely to saturate in about three weeks, before users notice. Which type of AI fits this use?
choices: Generative AI, because it creates new configuration text
Predictive AI using machine learning trained on historical telemetry
A static SNMP threshold that sends a Trap when utilization passes 90 percent
A northbound REST API on the controller
explanation: Predictive AI uses machine learning models trained on historical data to find patterns and forecast what will happen, such as capacity exhaustion or likely failures. Generative AI produces new content (text, configuration, summaries) from a prompt rather than forecasting from telemetry. A static threshold reacts only after the limit is crossed, and an API is an interface, not an analysis method.

stem: A script sends the request in the exhibit to a network controller and receives the response shown. Which two statements are true? (Choose two.)
exhibit:
POST /api/v1/vlans HTTP/1.1
Host: ctrl.corp.example
X-Auth-Token: eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOi...
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "vlan_id": 120,
  "name": "LAB",
  "description": "Test bench"
}

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: /api/v1/vlans/120
choices: The request performs a CRUD Create operation.
The script uses token-based authentication instead of sending a username and password in this request.
The 201 status code means the request failed because of a client error.
The request body is encoded in XML.
The request performs a CRUD Update that replaces an existing VLAN.
explanation: POST maps to Create, and 201 Created confirms the controller made the new resource (2xx codes mean success; 4xx means client error). The X-Auth-Token header carries a token the script obtained earlier, so credentials are not sent with each call. The Content-Type header and the braces show JSON, not XML, and replacing an existing resource would normally use PUT (Update).

stem: An inventory script worked at 09:00 but fails at 10:15, as shown in the exhibit. The URI, the account and the token value are unchanged. What is the most likely cause, and what should the script do?
exhibit:
09:00 $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "X-Auth-Token: $TOKEN" https://catc.corp.example/dna/intent/api/v1/network-device
200

10:15 $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "X-Auth-Token: $TOKEN" https://catc.corp.example/dna/intent/api/v1/network-device
401
choices: The resource no longer exists; the script should correct the URI.
The request is no longer authenticated, most likely because the token expired; the script should request a new token and retry.
The account is authenticated but lacks permission to read devices; an administrator must grant a role.
The controller had an internal failure; the script should wait for the server to recover.
explanation: 401 Unauthorized means the server did not accept the request's authentication. The same token worked earlier, and tokens are issued with a limited lifetime (60 minutes on Catalyst Center, and 75 minutes have passed), so the script should authenticate again (for example with a POST using Basic authentication) and use the new token. 404 Not Found would mean a missing resource, 403 Forbidden means the identity is known but not allowed, and 500 Internal Server Error is a server-side fault.

stem: Which statement correctly describes the tool and method that use the file in the exhibit?
exhibit:
- name: Standardize NTP on branch switches
  hosts: branch_switches
  gather_facts: no
  tasks:
    - name: Set NTP server
      cisco.ios.ios_config:
        lines:
          - ntp server 10.0.0.1
choices: It is a Terraform configuration written in HCL; Terraform compares it with its state file before applying the change.
It is a Puppet manifest; an agent on each switch pulls it from the Puppet server on a schedule.
It is an Ansible playbook written in YAML; a control node pushes the change over SSH, and no agent runs on the switches.
It is a Chef recipe written in Ruby; the chef-client on each switch converges to the new setting.
explanation: Ansible playbooks are YAML files of plays and tasks that use modules, such as cisco.ios.ios_config, and Ansible is agentless: the control node connects to IOS devices over SSH and pushes the change. Terraform uses declarative HCL files and a state file and is mainly used to provision infrastructure. Puppet manifests and Chef recipes are traditionally used with an agent on the managed node that pulls its configuration, and neither looks like this YAML.

stem: How many JSON objects does the exhibit contain? Count the outermost object.
explanation: An object is anything enclosed in curly braces. There is the outermost object, three objects inside the interfaces array, and the object that is the value of snmp, for five in total. The square brackets after interfaces and contacts are arrays, not objects, and values such as false and null are simple values.

stem: Based on the JSON in the exhibit, which two statements are true? (Choose two.)
exhibit:
{
  "device": "core-rtr-1",
  "mgmt_ip": "10.255.0.1",
  "asn": 65010,
  "bgp_enabled": "true",
  "neighbors": ["10.255.0.2", "10.255.0.3"],
  "location": null
}
choices: The value of bgp_enabled is a string, not a Boolean.
The value of asn is a number.
The value of neighbors is an object with two key/value pairs.
The location entry makes the data invalid, because null is not a JSON value.
The data is invalid, because JSON keys cannot contain underscores.
explanation: A value in double quotes is a string, so "true" is text; a Boolean would be written true without quotes. 65010 has no quotes, so it is a number. Square brackets make neighbors an array of two strings, not an object. null is a valid JSON value, and keys are any double-quoted strings, so underscores are allowed.

stem: A change board worries that an automation job pushing a new ACL to 600 routers would spread a single typo to every router at once. Which practice addresses that risk while keeping the benefits of automation?
choices: Return to applying the ACL manually at each router's CLI.
Keep the template under version control with peer review, run it first against a lab or a small pilot group, and verify before rolling out in stages.
Push to all 600 routers in parallel so the change window ends sooner.
Disable logging during the push so the job finishes faster.
explanation: Automation makes changes faster and more consistent, which also means an error spreads quickly, so good practice adds review, testing and staged rollout with verification. Going back to manual CLI work brings back slow changes and per-device mistakes. Pushing everywhere at once increases the impact of an error, and disabling logging removes the evidence needed to verify or troubleshoot the change.

stem: A campus is moving from box-by-box CLI management to a Catalyst Center managed SD-Access fabric. A colleague says the controller will take over routing and forward everyone's traffic. Which statement correctly describes what changes?
choices: All user traffic is sent to Catalyst Center, which looks up each flow and returns it to the correct switch.
The switches no longer run any control-plane protocols, so the underlay has no routing protocol.
Nothing changes, because controller-based networks still require engineers to configure each switch at the CLI.
The switches keep their own data planes and forward user traffic locally; the controller centralizes configuration, policy and monitoring and programs the switches through southbound interfaces.
explanation: Controller-based networking moves management and policy to a central controller, but the forwarding (data plane) stays on the devices, and in SD-Access the switches still run their own control-plane protocols, such as the underlay routing protocol (IS-IS when Catalyst Center automates the underlay). Catalyst Center is not in the data path, so fabric forwarding continues even if the controller is down. Sending every packet through the controller would not scale and is not how Catalyst Center works. The main operational change is that engineers express intent once on the controller instead of configuring each switch.

stem: In the exhibit, what type of API is used at interface B? Enter one word.
exhibit:
[ ITSM platform / Python scripts ]
              |
              |  (A) REST over HTTPS
              |
      [ Catalyst Center ]
              |
              |  (B) NETCONF, SSH, SNMP
              |
[ Switches, routers, WLCs ]
explanation: Interfaces from the controller down to the network devices are southbound APIs (for example NETCONF, RESTCONF, SSH, SNMP or OpenFlow). Interface A, from applications and scripts down to the controller, is the northbound API, usually REST with JSON.

stem: Which two statements correctly describe the underlay and overlay in a controller-based fabric such as SD-Access? (Choose two.)
choices: The underlay is the physical network and its routing, which provides IP reachability between the fabric devices.
The overlay uses tunnels, such as VXLAN, built over the underlay to carry endpoint traffic and keep segments separate.
The overlay must be built first, and the underlay is then created inside the overlay tunnels.
The underlay extends every user VLAN to every fabric switch over 802.1Q trunks with STP.
The fabric is only the cabling, and it has no control plane.
explanation: The underlay is the routed physical network (in SD-Access, routed links with IS-IS) that lets fabric devices reach each other's loopbacks. The overlay is the virtual network of tunnels on top of it, using VXLAN for data and LISP for endpoint location, and it carries segmentation. The underlay comes first because the overlay tunnels depend on it, SD-Access uses routed access rather than trunks and STP between fabric switches, and the fabric is not just cabling: it is the virtual overlay network built on the routed underlay, with its own control plane and data plane.

stem: An engineer asks a generative AI assistant to turn a plain-language request into an extended ACL for 30 branch routers. Which practice is most appropriate?
choices: Deploy the output directly, because generative AI returns the same verified answer every time.
Treat the output as a draft, then review and test it in a lab before deployment, because generative AI can produce configuration that looks correct but is wrong.
Use generative AI only to forecast link failures from telemetry, because that is its main purpose.
Skip testing, because machine learning models do not need training data and cannot be wrong.
explanation: Generative AI creates new content such as configuration, documentation or summaries from a prompt, and it can produce confident but incorrect output, so a human must review and test it like any other change. Its output is not guaranteed to be the same each time or to be verified. Forecasting failures from telemetry is predictive AI, and every machine learning model depends on training data.

stem: Match each REST API result to the HTTP status code the controller most likely returns.
pairs: A GET for the device list succeeds and returns the list in the body
A POST creates a new resource, and the response gives its URI in a Location header
A DELETE removes a VLAN and returns no body
A PUT is sent with malformed JSON in the body
A valid token for a read-only account is used to send a DELETE
A GET asks for a device ID that does not exist
explanation: 2xx codes mean success: 200 for a successful read or update with a body, 201 when a POST creates a resource, and 204 when the action worked and there is nothing to return. 4xx codes mean the client made an error: 400 for a request the server cannot parse, 403 when the caller is authenticated but not allowed, and 404 when the resource does not exist. 401 is different from 403: it means the request is not authenticated at all.

stem: A script must read the device inventory from a controller that uses token authentication. Put the steps in order.
items: The script sends a POST to the controller's authentication URI with the username and password in a Basic authentication header.
The controller checks the credentials and returns a token in a JSON response.
The script sends a GET for the inventory with the token in an X-Auth-Token header.
The controller validates the token and returns 200 OK with the inventory encoded as JSON.
The script parses the JSON and reads the values it needs.
explanation: Token-based REST APIs, such as the Catalyst Center API, first exchange credentials for a token (here with Basic authentication on a POST), then accept that token in a header on later calls until it expires. The response body is usually JSON, which the client then parses. Sending the GET before getting a token would return 401 Unauthorized.

stem: A team has two goals. Goal 1: declare cloud networks and firewalls in files, keep a record of what has been built, and preview every change before applying it. Goal 2: push day-to-day configuration changes over SSH to 300 existing IOS XE routers without installing software on them. Which pairing of tools fits best?
choices: Goal 1: Ansible. Goal 2: Terraform.
Goal 1: Terraform. Goal 2: Ansible.
Goal 1: Puppet. Goal 2: Chef.
Goal 1: Chef. Goal 2: Puppet.
explanation: Terraform is a declarative infrastructure-as-code tool that writes resources in HCL, tracks what exists in a state file, and shows a plan before apply, which matches Goal 1. Ansible is agentless and pushes changes over SSH using YAML playbooks, which matches Goal 2. Ansible keeps no state file, and Terraform does not push CLI changes over SSH. Puppet and Chef traditionally rely on an agent on each managed node that pulls its configuration, which conflicts with the no-installed-software requirement.

stem: A controller rejects the JSON in the exhibit with a parse error. Which line makes the data invalid?
exhibit:
1  {
 2    "site": "BOS-2",
 3    "floors": 4,
 4    "wifi": {"ssid": "CORP", "bands": ["2.4", "5", "6"]},
 5    "aps": [
 6      {"name": "ap-201", "poe": true},
 7      {"name": "ap-202", "poe": false},
 8    ],
 9    "notes": null
10  }
choices: Line 3, because numbers must be in double quotes
Line 4, because an object cannot contain an array
Line 7, because a comma follows the last element of the array
Line 9, because null must be written as a string
explanation: JSON does not allow a trailing comma after the last item in an array or object, so the comma after the ap-202 object on line 7 breaks parsing. Numbers are written without quotes, objects may contain arrays (and arrays may contain objects), and null is a valid literal written without quotes.

stem: Which statement accurately describes the JSON data in the exhibit?
choices: devices is an object that contains two arrays, one for each switch.
reachable is a string in the first device and a Boolean in the second.
The outermost object has two keys; devices is an array of two objects, and each location value is a nested object.
uplinks is an object whose keys are interface names.
explanation: The outermost braces hold two keys, devices and count. devices uses square brackets, so it is an array, and each element is an object in braces; location inside each is another object. reachable is the Boolean true or false in both entries (no quotes), and uplinks is an array of strings, not an object.

stem: Which two statements describe the role of a router in an enterprise network? (Choose two.)
choices: It forwards packets between different IP networks based on the destination IP address and its routing table.
It forwards frames based on destination MAC addresses that it learns from source MAC addresses.
Each of its interfaces is a separate broadcast domain, so it does not forward Layer 2 broadcasts between interfaces.
It floods packets for unknown destination networks out every interface except the one they arrived on.
All of its interfaces must be addressed in the same IP subnet so that hosts can reach it.
explanation: A router makes Layer 3 forwarding decisions: it matches the destination IP address against its routing table and forwards out the matching interface. Routers bound broadcast domains, so a broadcast received on one interface is not sent out the others. Learning MAC addresses and flooding unknown destinations is switch behavior; a router with no matching route (and no default route) drops the packet instead. Each router interface must be in a different subnet, not the same one.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. DSW1 is a Catalyst multilayer switch. A host in VLAN 10 uses 10.10.10.1 as its default gateway and sends a packet to a host in VLAN 20. What does DSW1 do with the packet?
exhibit:
DSW1# show running-config
(output omitted)
ip routing
!
interface Vlan10
 ip address 10.10.10.1 255.255.255.0
!
interface Vlan20
 ip address 10.10.20.1 255.255.255.0
!
DSW1# show ip route connected
(codes omitted)
      10.0.0.0/8 is variably subnetted, 4 subnets, 2 masks
C        10.10.10.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan10
L        10.10.10.1/32 is directly connected, Vlan10
C        10.10.20.0/24 is directly connected, Vlan20
L        10.10.20.1/32 is directly connected, Vlan20
choices: It floods the frame out every port in all VLANs because the destination is in a different VLAN.
It drops the packet because inter-VLAN routing requires an external router configured as a router on a stick.
It routes the packet between the two SVIs, rewrites the Ethernet header, and forwards it into VLAN 20.
It switches the frame at Layer 2 into VLAN 20 without changing the source MAC address.
explanation: With ip routing enabled and an SVI in each VLAN, a Layer 3 switch routes between the VLANs itself, usually in hardware. The connected routes for both subnets confirm it can reach VLAN 20 directly. Like any router, it builds a new Ethernet header with its own SVI MAC as the source, so the frame is not simply bridged unchanged. A router on a stick is only needed when the switch is Layer 2 only, and a switch never floods a frame into a different VLAN.

stem: A security team is replacing a traditional stateful firewall with a next-generation firewall (NGFW). Which capability does the NGFW add that the stateful firewall lacks?
choices: Tracking TCP session state so that return traffic for inside-initiated connections is permitted automatically
Identifying and controlling applications by inspecting traffic content, even when they use nonstandard ports
Translating inside private addresses to a public address with PAT
Permitting or denying traffic based on source and destination IP addresses and port numbers
explanation: Application visibility and control (deep inspection that recognizes the application regardless of port) is a defining NGFW feature, along with an integrated IPS, URL filtering and advanced malware protection. Stateful session tracking, NAT/PAT and filtering by address and port are features a traditional stateful firewall already provides, so they are not what the NGFW adds. An IPS, whether standalone or built into an NGFW, sits inline and can drop malicious traffic based on signatures.

stem: An autonomous access point advertises two SSIDs: CORP is mapped to VLAN 10 and GUEST is mapped to VLAN 99. The AP uplink connects to an 802.1Q trunk on the access switch. A wireless client on GUEST sends a frame to its default gateway. What does the AP do with the frame?
choices: It routes the packet from the wireless subnet to the VLAN 99 subnet using its own routing table.
It encapsulates the frame in a CAPWAP tunnel and sends it to the wireless LAN controller.
It translates the 802.11 frame to an 802.3 Ethernet frame, tags it with VLAN 99, and sends it out the trunk.
It sends the frame untagged on the native VLAN, and the switch places it in VLAN 99.
explanation: An access point is a Layer 2 bridge between the 802.11 wireless medium and the 802.3 wired network. An autonomous AP maps each SSID to a VLAN and tags the translated frame with that VLAN on the trunk, so GUEST traffic leaves tagged for VLAN 99. CAPWAP tunneling to a WLC is how a lightweight AP in local mode forwards traffic, not an autonomous AP. The AP does not route between subnets, and sending GUEST traffic untagged would place it in the native VLAN, not VLAN 99.

stem: Match each network component to its primary function.
pairs: Automates and monitors the enterprise network as an SDN controller with northbound REST APIs
Centrally configures lightweight APs and manages RF settings and client authentication
Bridges 802.11 clients to the network and tunnels their traffic to a controller in CAPWAP
Forwards frames within a VLAN using a MAC address table
Forwards packets between IP networks using a routing table
distractors: Inspects application content inline and blocks traffic that matches threat signatures
explanation: Catalyst Center is Cisco's enterprise SDN controller: it pushes intent-based configuration and provides assurance across switches, routers and wireless, with REST APIs for automation. A WLC manages lightweight APs (configuration, channel and power, client authentication) over CAPWAP. A Layer 2 switch forwards by MAC address within a VLAN, while a router forwards by IP address between networks. The extra description fits a next-generation firewall or IPS, not any of the listed components.

stem: Which group contains only endpoints?
choices: Desktop PC, Layer 2 switch, IP phone, tablet
IP phone, laptop, network printer, IP security camera
Smartphone, wireless LAN controller, printer, laptop
IP camera, router, tablet, desktop PC
explanation: Endpoints are the devices that originate or consume traffic at the edge of the network, such as PCs, laptops, phones, printers, cameras and IoT sensors. Switches, routers and wireless LAN controllers are network infrastructure that move or manage traffic for endpoints, so any group that contains one of them is wrong. Many endpoints (IP phones, cameras) draw power from the switch port through PoE, but that does not change their role.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. The capture was taken on a PC's access port. Which statement correctly identifies the roles of the hosts?
exhibit:
No.  Source        Destination   Protocol  Info
1    10.1.1.50     10.1.1.10     DNS       51544 > 53  Standard query A intranet.corp.local
2    10.1.1.10     10.1.1.50     DNS       53 > 51544  Standard query response A 10.1.2.25
3    10.1.1.50     10.1.2.25     TCP       51545 > 443 [SYN]
4    10.1.2.25     10.1.1.50     TCP       443 > 51545 [SYN, ACK]
5    10.1.1.50     10.1.2.25     TCP       51545 > 443 [ACK]
choices: 10.1.1.50 is a server because it initiates the connections to the other hosts.
10.1.1.10 is a DNS server, 10.1.2.25 is an HTTPS server, and 10.1.1.50 is the client.
10.1.2.25 is the DNS server and 10.1.1.10 is the web server.
10.1.1.10 is a DHCP server that assigned 10.1.2.25 to the client.
explanation: A server listens on a well-known port and answers requests; a client uses a random high (ephemeral) source port and starts the conversation. 10.1.1.10 answers on UDP 53 (DNS), and 10.1.2.25 accepts a TCP handshake on port 443 (HTTPS), so both are servers. 10.1.1.50 initiates both exchanges from ephemeral ports 51544 and 51545, which makes it the client. DHCP would use UDP ports 67 and 68, which do not appear.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. A new 802.3at (PoE+) access point is connected to Gi1/0/9 but never powers on. The other ports work normally. What is the most likely cause?
exhibit:
SW3# show power inline
Module   Available     Used     Remaining
          (Watts)     (Watts)    (Watts)
------   ---------   --------   ---------
1           370.0      357.6        12.4
Interface Admin  Oper       Power   Device              Class Max
                            (Watts)
--------- ------ ---------- ------- ------------------- ----- ----
Gi1/0/1   auto   on         30.0    Ieee PD             4     30.0
Gi1/0/2   auto   on         30.0    Ieee PD             4     30.0
(output omitted)
Gi1/0/8   auto   on         15.4    Ieee PD             3     30.0
Gi1/0/9   auto   power-deny 0.0     Ieee PD             4     30.0
choices: PoE is disabled on Gi1/0/9 because the Admin mode is auto instead of static.
The port maximum of 30 W is lower than the power an 802.3at device requires.
The switch did not detect a powered device on Gi1/0/9.
The switch has only 12.4 W left in its PoE budget, which is less than the class 4 allocation the AP needs.
explanation: The switch detected an IEEE powered device of class 4 on Gi1/0/9, but class 4 (802.3at) reserves up to 30 W at the switch port and only 12.4 W of the budget remains, so the port shows power-deny. The fix is more PoE budget (another power supply) or moving lower-priority devices. Admin mode auto is the default and means the port detects and powers devices automatically. 802.3at delivers up to 30 W at the PSE (about 25.5 W at the device), so a 30 W port maximum is sufficient, and the Device and Class columns show the PD was detected.

stem: A single-building campus has 12 access switches. Each access switch uplinks to a pair of Catalyst switches, and that same pair also connects to the WAN edge routers and the data center. Which design is this?
choices: Three-tier campus design
Spine-leaf design
Two-tier campus design with a collapsed core
Hub-and-spoke WAN design
explanation: In a two-tier (collapsed core) design, the distribution and core layers are combined into one pair of switches that aggregate the access layer and also connect to the rest of the network. It suits a single building or small campus where a separate core adds cost without benefit. A three-tier design adds a dedicated core layer that interconnects multiple distribution blocks. Spine-leaf is a data center design, and hub-and-spoke describes WAN site connectivity.

stem: Match each layer of the three-tier campus design to its role.
pairs: Connects endpoints and provides PoE, port security and VLAN assignment
Aggregates access switches and is the boundary for routing and policy between VLANs
High-speed backbone that interconnects distribution blocks with minimal policy
distractors: Connects the hosts in a data center fabric with a fixed two-hop path between any two leaf switches
explanation: The access layer is where users, phones, APs and printers attach, so features such as PoE, port security and access VLANs live there. The distribution layer aggregates access switches and typically provides inter-VLAN routing, redundancy and policy. The core is a fast, highly available transport between distribution blocks and should avoid CPU-intensive policy. The distractor describes a spine-leaf data center fabric, not a campus layer.

stem: Which two statements describe a spine-leaf architecture? (Choose two.)
choices: Every leaf switch connects to every spine switch.
Spine switches connect to each other in a full mesh to carry east-west traffic.
Servers, storage and other endpoints connect to leaf switches, not to spine switches.
Leaf switches connect directly to other leaf switches to shorten the path between servers.
The number of hops between two servers depends on which leaf switches they are attached to.
explanation: In spine-leaf, each leaf has a link to every spine, spines do not connect to each other, and leaves do not connect to each other. Endpoints attach only to leaves, so traffic between any two servers on different leaves always crosses exactly leaf, spine, leaf. That consistent path is what makes latency predictable for heavy east-west traffic in data centers. Adding spine or leaf switches scales the fabric without redesigning it.

stem: A branch office router has two separate circuits to the same Internet service provider so that one circuit can fail without losing Internet access. Which WAN connectivity option is this?
choices: Single-homed
Dual-homed
Multihomed
Dual multihomed
explanation: Dual-homed means two connections to the same ISP, which protects against a link failure but not an ISP-wide outage. Single-homed is one link to one ISP. Multihomed is one link to each of two (or more) different ISPs, and dual multihomed is two links to each of two different ISPs, which gives the most redundancy.

stem: Which statement best describes a typical small office/home office (SOHO) network?
choices: A dedicated core layer interconnects separate distribution switch pairs.
One integrated device usually provides routing, switching, wireless access, firewall and DHCP/NAT functions, with a broadband link to the ISP.
Each access point is managed by an on-site wireless LAN controller.
Servers connect to leaf switches that uplink to every spine switch.
explanation: A SOHO network is small, so a single consumer or small-business router usually combines a router, a small switch, a wireless AP, a basic firewall, a DHCP server and NAT, connecting through cable, DSL or fiber broadband. Dedicated core layers, on-site WLCs and spine-leaf fabrics belong to campus and data center designs, not SOHO.

stem: A company is comparing on-premises infrastructure with a public cloud service. Which two are essential characteristics of cloud computing as defined by NIST? (Choose two.)
choices: On-demand self-service, so the customer provisions resources without a human at the provider
Hardware dedicated to one customer and purchased up front to handle peak demand
Rapid elasticity, so capacity can grow and shrink quickly with demand
Access only through a dedicated private WAN circuit to the provider
Resources located in the customer's own data center
explanation: NIST lists five essential characteristics: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity and measured service. Buying hardware up front and sizing it for peak demand is the on-premises model, which is a capital expense; cloud is usually paid as an operating expense based on usage. Cloud services are reachable over many network types including the Internet (a private WAN link is optional), and resources run in the provider's data centers through shared pooling, not in the customer's own facility.

stem: Two buildings on a campus are 8 km apart. The engineer needs a 10-Gbps link between their distribution switches. Which option meets the requirement?
choices: 10GBASE-SR optics over OM4 multimode fiber
10GBASE-LR optics over single-mode fiber
10GBASE-T over Category 6a UTP
10GBASE-SR optics over OM3 multimode fiber
explanation: Single-mode fiber has a small core and uses a laser, so it supports long distances; 10GBASE-LR is specified for up to 10 km. Multimode fiber with 10GBASE-SR reaches only about 300 m on OM3 and about 400 m on OM4 because the wider core causes modal dispersion. Copper 10GBASE-T over Cat 6a is limited to 100 m.

stem: Which statement correctly compares shared-media Ethernet with point-to-point Ethernet links?
choices: On a hub (shared media), several devices can transmit at the same time without collisions.
A switch port connected to a hub should be set to full duplex for best performance.
On a full-duplex point-to-point link between a switch and a host, CSMA/CD is not used and collisions cannot occur.
Point-to-point Ethernet links require a crossover cable, while shared-media links use straight-through cables.
explanation: A hub repeats every signal to all ports, so all attached devices share one collision domain and must run half duplex with CSMA/CD. A full-duplex point-to-point link (for example a switch port to a PC) has separate transmit and receive pairs and only two devices, so collisions are impossible and CSMA/CD is disabled. A port connected to a hub must be half duplex, otherwise a duplex mismatch occurs. Cable choice is about pinouts, and modern Cisco switches use auto-MDIX, so it does not define shared versus point-to-point.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. Users connected through SW2 report slow file transfers across the link to SW1. Which two statements are true? (Choose two.)
exhibit:
SW1# show interfaces FastEthernet0/12
FastEthernet0/12 is up, line protocol is up (connected)
  Hardware is Fast Ethernet, address is 0019.e86a.6f8c (bia 0019.e86a.6f8c)
  MTU 1500 bytes, BW 100000 Kbit/sec, DLY 100 usec,
  Half-duplex, 100Mb/s, media type is 10/100BaseTX
(output omitted)
     1874653 packets input, 241736412 bytes, 0 no buffer
     0 runts, 0 giants, 0 throttles
     0 input errors, 0 CRC, 0 frame, 0 overrun, 0 ignored
     1765201 packets output, 225129876 bytes, 0 underruns
     1408 output errors, 3215 collisions, 2 interface resets
     0 babbles, 1408 late collision, 0 deferred

SW2# show interfaces FastEthernet0/1
FastEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up (connected)
  Full-duplex, 100Mb/s, media type is 10/100BaseTX
(output omitted)
     1791377 packets input, 228416520 bytes, 0 no buffer
     1655 runts, 0 giants, 0 throttles
     2310 input errors, 2290 CRC, 0 frame, 0 overrun, 0 ignored
     0 output errors, 0 collisions, 0 interface resets
     0 babbles, 0 late collision, 0 deferred
choices: There is a duplex mismatch between SW1 Fa0/12 and SW2 Fa0/1.
SW2 Fa0/1 is the interface operating in half duplex.
The runts and CRC errors on SW2 occur because SW1 stops sending frames partway through when it senses a collision.
Setting the speed to 100 on both interfaces will clear the errors.
The cable is longer than 100 meters and must be replaced.
explanation: SW1 runs half duplex and SW2 runs full duplex, which is a duplex mismatch. SW2 transmits whenever it wants, so SW1 sees collisions, including late collisions (after the first 64 bytes), and aborts its own frames. Those aborted frames arrive at SW2 as runts and frames with bad FCS, which is why SW2 counts CRC and input errors. Both sides already run 100 Mb/s, so the speed is not the problem; set both ends to auto (or both to full duplex). Late collisions can also come from an over-length cable, but with one side full and one half, the mismatch is the cause.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. The input error counters on Gi1/0/5 increase steadily. What is the most likely cause?
exhibit:
SW4# show interfaces GigabitEthernet1/0/5
GigabitEthernet1/0/5 is up, line protocol is up (connected)
  Hardware is Gigabit Ethernet, address is 7c21.0e4a.1b05 (bia 7c21.0e4a.1b05)
  MTU 1500 bytes, BW 1000000 Kbit/sec, DLY 10 usec,
  Full-duplex, 1000Mb/s, media type is 10/100/1000BaseTX
(output omitted)
     4826113 packets input, 3170553214 bytes, 0 no buffer
     0 runts, 0 giants, 0 throttles
     5874 input errors, 5874 CRC, 0 frame, 0 overrun, 0 ignored
     4102988 packets output, 1903311420 bytes, 0 underruns
     0 output errors, 0 collisions, 0 interface resets
     0 babbles, 0 late collision, 0 deferred
choices: A duplex mismatch with the attached device
A speed mismatch with the attached device
A damaged cable, poor termination or electrical interference on the link
A broadcast storm in the VLAN
explanation: CRC errors mean frames arrived with a frame check sequence that did not match, so the bits were corrupted in transit. With full duplex at 1000 Mb/s, no collisions and no runts, the usual cause is the physical layer: a bad or over-long cable, a bad connector or patch panel, or EMI. A duplex mismatch would show collisions and late collisions on the half-duplex side, and a speed mismatch normally keeps the link down. A broadcast storm raises traffic counters, not CRC errors.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. The PC on Fa0/7 has its NIC left at the default autonegotiation setting. The cable was replaced and tested good, but CRC errors and runts keep increasing on Fa0/7. What is the cause?
exhibit:
SW5# show running-config interface FastEthernet0/7
interface FastEthernet0/7
 description PC-Finance-07
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 30
 speed 100
 duplex full
end

SW5# show interfaces FastEthernet0/7 | include duplex|runts|CRC
  Full-duplex, 100Mb/s, media type is 10/100BaseTX
     214 runts, 0 giants, 0 throttles
     1532 input errors, 1499 CRC, 0 frame, 0 overrun, 0 ignored
choices: The PC cannot detect the speed without autonegotiation, so it falls back to 10 Mb/s.
Manually setting speed and duplex disables autonegotiation on Fa0/7, so the PC detects 100 Mb/s but defaults to half duplex.
The PC negotiated full duplex with the switch, so the errors must come from the PC's NIC driver.
The switch port should be configured as a trunk because the PC is in VLAN 30.
explanation: When both speed and duplex are hard-coded on a Cisco switch port, the port stops autonegotiating. The autonegotiating PC can still sense the speed from the signal, but IEEE rules make it default to half duplex at 10 or 100 Mb/s. The result is a duplex mismatch: the full-duplex switch side counts CRC errors and runts from frames the PC aborts on collisions. Fix it by setting both ends to auto (Cisco recommended) or both to 100/full. Speed is still detected correctly, and an access port in VLAN 30 is correct for a PC.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. The uplink between SW1 and SW2 went down right after an engineer changed the configuration on SW2 Gi1/0/24. The cable has not changed. What is the most likely cause?
exhibit:
SW1# show interfaces status | include Gi1/0/24
Port      Name           Status       Vlan  Duplex  Speed Type
Gi1/0/24  uplink-to-SW2  notconnect   1       full    100 10/100/1000BaseTX

SW1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24 | include speed|duplex
 speed 100
 duplex full

SW2# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24 | include speed|duplex
 speed 1000
 duplex full
choices: A duplex mismatch, because duplex mismatches bring the link down
A speed mismatch, because both ends are manually set to different speeds
Port security shut down the interface on SW1
A native VLAN mismatch on the trunk
explanation: Both ends are hard-coded to different speeds (100 and 1000 Mb/s), so the link cannot come up and the port shows notconnect. Set both ends to the same speed or back to auto. A duplex mismatch does not take the link down; it stays up with collisions and CRC errors. A port security violation would show err-disabled, and a native VLAN mismatch produces CDP log messages but does not drop the physical link.

stem: Which three are characteristics of TCP? (Choose three.)
choices: It sets up a connection with a three-way handshake before sending data.
It uses sequence numbers and acknowledgments to recover lost segments.
It uses windowing to provide flow control.
It has a fixed 8-byte header.
It is preferred for real-time voice and video because it never retransmits.
It provides best-effort delivery with no acknowledgments.
explanation: TCP is connection oriented (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK), reliable (sequencing, acknowledgments and retransmission) and provides flow control through a sliding window. The 8-byte header, no retransmission and best-effort delivery describe UDP. Real-time voice and video normally use UDP (RTP) because a late retransmitted packet is useless and the lower overhead keeps delay down.

stem: Match each application to the transport protocol and port it normally uses.
explanation: SSH uses TCP 22 and HTTPS uses TCP 443. Standard DNS queries use UDP 53 (TCP 53 is used for zone transfers and large responses). DHCP servers listen on UDP 67 and clients on UDP 68, SNMP agents are polled on UDP 161 (traps go to UDP 162), and TFTP uses UDP 69. TCP 23 is Telnet and UDP 514 is syslog.

stem: A host is configured with IP address 172.16.45.200/21. What is the subnet ID (network address) of the subnet the host is in?
explanation: A /21 mask is 255.255.248.0, so the interesting octet is the third, with a block size of 256 - 248 = 8. The multiples of 8 near 45 are 40 and 48, so the host is in 172.16.40.0/21. That subnet runs from 172.16.40.0 to the broadcast 172.16.47.255, with usable hosts 172.16.40.1 to 172.16.47.254.

stem: What is the broadcast address of the subnet that contains host 10.20.30.77 with mask 255.255.255.224?
explanation: 255.255.255.224 is /27, which gives a block size of 32 in the fourth octet. The subnets are .0, .32, .64, .96 and so on, so .77 is in 10.20.30.64/27. The broadcast address is one less than the next subnet: 10.20.30.95. Usable hosts are 10.20.30.65 to 10.20.30.94.

stem: What is the last usable host address in the subnet that contains 192.168.10.130/26?
explanation: A /26 has a block size of 64, so the subnets are .0, .64, .128 and .192. Host .130 is in 192.168.10.128/26, whose broadcast is 192.168.10.191. The last usable host is one less than the broadcast: 192.168.10.190. The first usable host is 192.168.10.129.

stem: A VLAN must support 500 hosts. What is the longest subnet mask (the fewest wasted addresses) that supports it? Enter it in dotted-decimal format.
explanation: You need host bits h where 2^h - 2 is at least 500. With 8 host bits you get only 254 usable addresses; with 9 host bits you get 510. Nine host bits leaves 23 network bits, so the mask is /23, which is 255.255.254.0. A /22 would also work but wastes addresses, and a /24 is too small.

stem: The block 10.50.0.0/16 is divided into equal-size subnets. Each subnet must support at least 1000 hosts, and the design must create as many subnets as possible. How many subnets result?
explanation: 1000 hosts need 10 host bits (2^10 - 2 = 1022); 9 bits would give only 510. Ten host bits means a /22 mask (255.255.252.0). Going from /16 to /22 borrows 6 bits, so there are 2^6 = 64 subnets: 10.50.0.0/22, 10.50.4.0/22, and so on up to 10.50.252.0/22.

stem: Which two addresses are valid host addresses in subnet 10.1.8.0/22? (Choose two.)
explanation: A /22 has a block size of 4 in the third octet, so 10.1.8.0/22 covers 10.1.8.0 through 10.1.11.255. 10.1.8.0 is the subnet ID and 10.1.11.255 is the broadcast, so neither can be assigned. 10.1.10.0 looks like a network address but is in the middle of the range and is a valid host, as is 10.1.11.254 (the last usable). 10.1.12.1 belongs to the next subnet and 10.1.7.255 to the previous one.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. The engineer allocates subnets from 192.168.50.0/24 with VLSM, largest requirement first, each subnet as small as possible and starting at the lowest available address. What subnet ID and prefix length are assigned to LAN C? Enter it in the format a.b.c.d/nn.
exhibit:
Address block: 192.168.50.0/24
LAN A   100 hosts
LAN B    50 hosts
LAN C    20 hosts
WAN 1     2 hosts (point-to-point)
WAN 2     2 hosts (point-to-point)
explanation: LAN A needs 100 hosts, so it gets a /25 (126 usable): 192.168.50.0/25. LAN B needs 50, so a /26 (62 usable): 192.168.50.128/26. LAN C needs 20, so a /27 (30 usable): the next free block is 192.168.50.192/27. The WAN links then take /30s at 192.168.50.224/30 and 192.168.50.228/30. Allocating largest first keeps every block on its natural boundary and avoids overlaps.

stem: Refer to the exhibit. PC-7 cannot ping its default gateway. What is the cause?
exhibit:
R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.1.94 255.255.255.224
 duplex auto
 speed auto
end

PC-7 IPv4 settings
  IPv4 address . . . : 192.168.1.97
  Subnet mask  . . . : 255.255.255.224
  Default gateway  . : 192.168.1.94
choices: 192.168.1.94 is the broadcast address of its subnet, so it cannot be used on a router interface.
192.168.1.97 is the network address of PC-7's subnet.
PC-7 is in subnet 192.168.1.96/27, but the gateway address is in subnet 192.168.1.64/27.
